# Anti-Replay Design

The `tbft_principal_verify_mac_in_with_replay_check` function ships with a
deliberate no-op where timestamp-based anti-replay logic would otherwise live.
This document explains why that is intentional, what replaces the missing
check, and why the substitution is sufficient for TinyBFT's deployment model.

## Overview

PBFT and its derivatives traditionally defend against replay attacks by
recording the timestamp of every accepted message and rejecting subsequent
messages whose timestamps are older than the latest. TinyBFT's
`tbft_principal_verify_mac_in_with_replay_check` accepts the `msg_time_us`
parameter but throws it away. Two replacement mechanisms — HMAC session key
rotation and per-certificate sender bitmaps — together provide equivalent
guarantees without depending on synchronised clocks across the embedded
cluster.

## tbft_principal_verify_mac_in_with_replay_check

The function lives at `src/tbft_principal.c:302`. It accepts four arguments:

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|-----------|------|---------|
| `p` | `tbft_principal_t *` | Sender's per-peer crypto state (carries the current HMAC in-key) |
| `msg` | `const void *` | Message body to verify |
| `msg_len` | `size_t` | Length of `msg` |
| `mac` | `const tbft_mac_t *` | HMAC authenticator supplied with the message |
| `msg_time_us` | `int64_t` | Sender's monotonic timestamp at send time (unused) |

Behaviour:

1. Calls `tbft_principal_verify_mac_in` (`src/tbft_principal.c:281`) to
   verify the HMAC-SHA256 authenticator against the current
   `psa_hmac_in_id` key. On failure, returns `false` after logging the
   first four MAC bytes at `WARN` level.
2. Returns `true` on successful MAC verification — the timestamp parameter
   is intentionally ignored.

## The (void)msg_time_us; return true; pattern

The full body of the function (excluding the MAC-failure log path) is:

```c
    /* Anti-replay check disabled: nodes boot at different times so their
     * esp_timer_get_time() values are offset by minutes. The HMAC key is
     * rotated on every New_key exchange (verified by the self-test), which
     * provides replay protection — an old message under a rotated key fails
     * HMAC verification. */
    (void)msg_time_us;
    return true;
```

This appears at `src/tbft_principal.c:320-321`. The `(void)msg_time_us;`
cast silences the unused-parameter warning and makes the no-op explicit.
`return true;` short-circuits the freshness check that would otherwise
compare `msg_time_us` against `p->last_auth_time_us`.

## Problem 1: Staggered boot (esp_timer_get_time starts at 0)

`esp_timer_get_time()` returns microseconds since boot. Each ESP32 board's
counter resets to zero on every power cycle. A typical deployment procedure
is:

```text
flash board 1 -> power on -> board 1 boot at t=0
... wait while operator flashes board 2 ... (minutes)
flash board 2 -> power on -> board 2 boot at t=0
```

When board 2 sends a Pre-prepare to board 1, its `timestamp_us` is
"minutes old" relative to board 1's local timer. A naive monotonicity check
(`msg_time_us > last_auth_time_us`) would reject the message because
"minutes ago" is less than "seconds ago" from board 1's perspective.

## Problem 2: 5-minute slack is one-directional

A defender might propose adding a fixed future-tolerance window. The codebase
defines such a constant at `src/tbft_principal.c:32-34`:

```c
#ifndef TBFT_ANTI_REPLAY_FUTURE_SLACK_US
#define TBFT_ANTI_REPLAY_FUTURE_SLACK_US  ((int64_t)300 * 1000 * 1000)
#endif
```

The slack only helps when the receiver's clock is ahead of the sender's.
It cannot help in the reverse direction: if a freshly-booted board's
"now" is minutes behind a long-running board's "now", every message from
the freshly-booted board appears stale. A 5-minute window covers
short-cycle flashing but breaks down the moment any single board sits
unpowered for longer.

NTP-style synchronisation is unavailable on the cluster: there is no
infrastructure for time distribution, and the application layer does
not depend on real wall-clock time.

## Replacement: Key rotation (New_key + esp_fill_random)

`tbft_principal_set_in_key` (`src/tbft_principal.c:324`) installs a new
HMAC session key and runs a self-test that computes a MAC with a fresh
key, verifies it, and only then sets `p->keys_fresh = true`. The
self-test guarantees the new key is wired correctly.

Replay attack analysis with this primitive:

```text
attacker captures Pre_prepare P under key K_old
attacker waits
attacker replays P
... cluster has rotated to K_new ...
receiver verifies HMAC with K_new
   MAC(P, K_new) != MAC(P, K_old)  -> verification FAILS
   -> P rejected as if it were a forgery
```

The captured message is no longer a valid authenticator. The protection
is automatic: every `New_key` exchange — and the broadcast loop in
`tbft_replica_run` at `src/tbft_replica.c:362-379` re-broadcasts ours
every 5-60 seconds — invalidates the entire set of pre-rotation
authenticators.

`tbft_principal_set_in_key` additionally resets `p->last_auth_time_us = 0`
(`src/tbft_principal.c:377`) so the unused watermark starts at a known
value for the new key stream.

## Replacement: Sender bitmap (per-cert duplicate guard)

The agreement region tracks per-sender contributions to each Prepare and
Commit certificate with a `tbft_bitmap_t` (a 64-bit integer). The
duplicate-detection code at `src/tbft_replica.c:1188-1192`:

```c
    if (tbft_bitmap_test(&sl->prepared_cert.pc.bmap, sender)) {
        ESP_LOGD(TAG, "prepare: duplicate from replica %d seqno=%lld",
                 sender, (long long)prep->seqno);
        return;
    }
```

The same pattern applies to Commit at `src/tbft_replica.c:1298-1302`.
A replayed message from the same sender, for the same sequence number,
fails this test and is dropped before reaching the certificate logic.
Cross-replica replay is impossible because the bitmap is keyed by sender.

## Why HMAC over full message (incl. seqno) provides cross-seqno protection

The HMAC authenticator is computed over the full message body including
`hdr.seqno` (the field embedded in `tbft_msg_hdr_t`). An attacker cannot
replay a Prepare for seqno=5 as a Prepare for seqno=6: even with the
same key, the HMAC bytes differ, and the receiver recomputes the MAC over
the actual seqno field of the received message.

This is also why the bitmap duplicate check is sound: two Prepare
messages with the same sender id, same view, and same seqno must have
identical MACs (or one is a forgery), and only one of them can satisfy
HMAC verification at a time.

## Do not re-enable warning

> Do NOT re-enable timestamp-based anti-replay without solving the
> staggered-boot clock synchronisation problem first.

The cluster runs without an NTP source, without RTC synchronisation, and
without a designated time-master. Any monotonicity check on
`msg_time_us` will reject legitimate messages from any node that booted
later than the receiver. A future change to add a real-time clock
backed by a battery or external synchronisation source would unlock
timestamp-based anti-replay, but only if the change also covers the
*reverse* case (late sender, early receiver) — a 5-minute slack does
not suffice.
